question.problem: Emma earns $$19,500$ a year. Of this amount, she must pay $12.6%$ in taxes. How much money should Emma pay in taxes?
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we can use the formula:

$$
\text{part}=\text{percentage}\times \text{whole}
$$

In our case, the whole is the amount of money Emma earns annually, which is $$19,500.$ The percentage is $12.6%,$ and the part is the amount she must pay in taxes.

**Method 1**

First, we convert the percentage to a decimal:

$$
12.6%=12.6÷100=0.126
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =12.6%\times 19,500 \\  & =0.126\times 19,500 \\  & =2,457\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $12.6%$ of $19,500$ is $2,457.$ Hence, Emma must pay $$2,457$ in taxes.

**Method 2**

First, we convert the percentage to a fraction:

$$
12.6%=\frac{12.6}{100}
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =12.6%\times 19,500 \\  & =\frac{12.6}{100}\times 19,500 \\  & =12.6\times \frac{19,500}{100} \\  & =12.6\times 195 \\  & =2,457\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $12.6%$ of $19,500$ is $2,457.$ Hence, Emma must pay $$2,457$ in taxes.
